The correct formula is NI = NNP - indirect taxes + subsidies.

National Income (NI) is essentially Net National Product (NNP) at factor cost. To get from NNP at market price to NNP at factor cost (which is NI):

Subtract indirect taxes: Indirect taxes are included in the market price of goods and services, but they are not part of the income earned by the factors of production.

Add subsidies: Subsidies are payments made by the government to producers, which reduce their costs and thus effectively increase the income they earn. They are not reflected in market prices.

Depreciation is already accounted for in the calculation of Net National Product (NNP) from Gross National Product (GNP). NNP is GNP minus depreciation. Therefore, it is not part of the calculation of NI from NNP

NutritionActivities
AutotrophsSynthesize their own organic food.
SaprotrophsFeed on dead organic matter
SymbiontsUse food from other living organisms with which they are associated for mutual benefit.
ParasitesAbsorb food from living organisms and cause harm to them.

Further insights:

Autotrophs are organisms that can produce their own food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide through a process called photosynthesis. Plants are the most common example. They are self-sufficient in terms of food production.

Saprotrophs are organisms that obtain their nutrients from dead and decaying organic matter (like dead plants, animals, and waste products). They play a crucial role as decomposers in ecosystems. Fungi and some bacteria are examples of saprotrophs.

Symbionts live in close association with another organism (often of a different species) and typically both organisms benefit from the relationship. This is a broad category, and the specific type of nutritional relationship can vary. However, the key idea is that they rely on another living organism for food (or other resources). It's important to note that unlike parasites, symbionts generally have a mutually beneficial relationship with their host.

Parasites are organisms that live on or in another living organism (the host) and derive their food at the host's expense. They benefit, but the host is harmed in some way. Tapeworms and ticks are examples of parasites.

Vitamin K is one of the fat-soluble vitamins. It helps with blood clotting.

The major source of vitamin K is found in green plants. This form is called phylloquinone. Another form of vitamin K is made by bacteria living in the intestine. This form is called menaquinone. The synthetic form of vitamin K is called menadione. This form is the most potent. It has two times the activity of phylloquinone.

Vitamin K is used to prevent and treat certain blood clotting (coagulation) issues. It's also used to prevent severe bleeding (hemorrhagic disease) in newborns.

In 1820, a Danish physicist, Hans Christian Oersted, discovered that there was a relationship between electricity and magnetism. By setting up a compass through a wire carrying an electric current, Oersted showed that moving electrons can create a magnetic field.

Further insights:

Benjamin Franklin: Known for his work with electricity, including the famous kite experiment, but he did not discover electromagnetism.

James Clerk Maxwell: Formulated the theory of electromagnetism and unified electricity, magnetism, and light into a single framework, but this was later in the 19th century.

Andre-Marie Ampere: Contributed significantly to the study of electromagnetism, particularly in understanding the relationship between electric currents and magnetic fields, but he built upon Oersted's discovery.

Invasion of Nadir Shah (1739): He was the Persian emperor who attacked India in 1738-39 during the period of Muhammad Shah. He defeated the Mughal army at the Battle of Karnal (1739) and looted Delhi. Nadir Shah's invasion made India vulnerable to the attacks from the North-West region.

Ahmad Shah Abdali (1748): He was the successor of Nadir Shah after the latter got assassinated during a rebellion in 1747. He invaded India seven times between 1748 and 1767 and captured Delhi. In 1761, Abdali defeated the Marathas in the third battle of Panipat.

Third battle of Panipat (1761): It was fought between the Ahmad Shah Abdali and the Marathas. It ended the Maratha attempt to succeed the Mughals as rulers of India and marked the virtual end of the Mughal empire.

The Battle of Buxar (1764): It was fought on October 1764, between East India Company, led by Hector Munro, and the combined armies of Mir Qasim, Nawab of Bengal till 1764; the Nawab of Awadh Shuja-ud-Daula; and the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II. It was a decisive victory for the British East India Company. The war had been brought to an end by the Treaty of Allahabad in 1765.

Source: NCERT

Gopalhari Deshmukh (1823-1892) was a social reformer and rationalist from Maharashtra. He held the post of a judge under British raj, but wrote for a weekly Prabhakar under the pen name of Lokahitawadi on social reform issues.

He advocated a reorganisation of Indian society on rational principles and modern, humanistic, secular values.

He attacked Hindu orthodoxy and supported social and religious equality. He wrote against the evils of the caste system.

He said, "If religion does not sanction social reform, then change religion." He started a weekly, Hitechhu, and also played a leading role in founding the periodicals, Gyan Prakash, Indu Prakash and Lokahitawadi.

Source: Modern India by Rajiv Ahir

Total internal reflection occurs when light passes from a denser medium to a rarer medium.

When light travels from a denser medium (like water or glass) to a rarer medium (like air), it bends away from the normal (the line perpendicular to the surface). As the angle of incidence increases, the angle of refraction also increases.

At a certain angle (the critical angle), the angle of refraction becomes 90 degrees, and the refracted ray travels along the interface between the two media.

Beyond this critical angle, the light is no longer refracted but is instead reflected back into the denser medium. This is total internal reflection.

Satavahana kingdom was divided into subdivisions called aharas or rashtras, meaning districts.

The lowest level of administration was a grama which was under the charge of a Gramika.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. a) greeted him gladly, his wife and

b) children were very happy because

c) when Regulus came to Rome, all the people

d) they thought that they would not be parted again.
questions.solution:
Part 'c' is the opening part of the sentence as it introduces the person 'Regulus'. Hence, option (c) is correct.

A positive degree of adjective/adverb is used before 'enough'. So, the use of 'better/best/fairer/finest' is incorrect. So, 'good' will be used here.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Los Angeles is the ten most populous city in the world, and it continues to expand like anything.

Los Angeles is the ten most populous city in the world, and it continues to expand like anything.

options.text: Los Angeles is the ten most
options.html: Los Angeles is the ten most

questions.solution:
The error lies in option (a).

When numbers are used as adjectives, they are used in the following manner.

Ordinal numbers- first, second, third, tenth.

The correct sequence is: ordinal number + noun.

For example: Open your book on the fifth page.

Similarly, in this context, 'tenth' (ordinal number) should replace 'ten' (cardinal number) as 'city' is a noun. As the number comes before the noun, it should be ordinal.

Thus, the error is in option (a) Los Angeles is the ten most.

Therefore, the corrected form of the sentence is: Los Angeles is the tenth most populous city in the world, and it continues to expand like anything.

Additional Information:

Cardinal numbers- one, two, three.

The correct sequence is: noun + cardinal number.

For example: The child studies in class three.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ['be' here] and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Future Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

For example:

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb [be] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

These types of questions contain Modal verbs. Some of the modal verbs are: Can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, ought to.

The format of such a sentence in Active Voice is: Subject + Modal + V1 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + Modal + be + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

You can do this. (Active Voice)

This can be done by you. (Passive Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is (c): The money may be fetched by the messengers.
